Definition: from G5228 and G906; to throw beyod the usual mark, i.e. (figuratively) to surpass (only active participle supereminent):--exceeding, excel, pass.
BiblicalUsage: hyperbállō means to throw beyond, to surpass, to excel. In 2 Corinthians 3:10, the text says "by reason of the glory that excelleth." In 2 Corinthians 9:14, the text says "which long after you for the exceeding grace of God in you."
TheologicalSignificance: What hyperbállō teaches me is that grace is God giving what we could never earn, and never taking it back. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
